scope: CRITICAL: state 10 is reached WITHOUT any snapshot parse, so 'state 10' was never proof that a snapshot was accepted

run.gamestate: sent as usual (--gamestate-source native, native gamestate payload)
run.snapshots: queued by the game server every 2 s with --snapshot-delay 20

the_finding: the client reached network state 10 with ZERO calls into the snapshot parser (0x471980 / 0x471BB3 never fired)
so state 10 is produced by the GAMESTATE alone, not by processing a snapshot

therefore every conclusion of the form 'body X reaches state 10, so the snapshot was accepted' is INVALID - including the baseline 'hybrid 167-byte body reaches state 10' that this project has treated as its ground truth since early rounds
what_state_10_actually_means: most likely: the client finished the load handshake and entered the in-match network state, with cgame alive but with no scene data - which also explains why the frame is black
it does NOT mean a snapshot was parsed, validated, and applied
implications: the only reliable oracle for snapshot parsing is the breakpoint evidence (snap_trace / stream_error at 0x4724A5), not the network state
the rounds that used state 10 as an accept signal (roughly 60-140) measured the wrong thing, although their breakpoint-based measurements remain valid where traces exist
the 'rejection' results that DID show stream_error = 1 were real rejections of the parse; the 'acceptance' results that showed state 10 without traces were not acceptances at all
what_to_check_next: confirm that the snapshot parser fires at all in a run where the snapshot actually arrives (i.e. traces > 0 with the same body): if it never fires, the snapshots may not be reaching the client at all, which would re-contextualise the last two rounds entirely
verify the forward/ring bridge path end-to-end with the delivery assertion plus a non-zero snap_trace count before drawing any further conclusion
